title: Tests for finding bugs
historical_note: English translation of the historical record as of 2026-10-16. Counts and implementation status below describe that record, not the current repository. The original Japanese document remains unchanged.
content_lines: # Tests for finding bugs
`test_adversarial_models.py` loads official case packs, validates inputs against their contracts,
and compares model results with independently specified expected bit patterns.
Rounding-mode tests explicitly derive validation contracts, including regression expectations, from official cases.
They target bugs that ordinary fixtures miss when both sides use the same model.
Expected values use neither the target model nor host floating-point arithmetic.
Run from the project root. No additional Python dependencies are required.
```sh
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_adversarial_models.py -v
## 2026-10-16: Added boundary and failure-path tests throughout the project
Python tests increased from **527 → 1,186 methods (659 added)**.
Both ordinary `unittest discover` and `check --quality` run the new files automatically.
| New file | Methods | Main checks |
| `test_validation_boundaries.py` | 307 | JSON/YAML, atomic-write failures, Python case extraction, memory/immediates, ISA cycles and long references, configuration, deterministic generation |
| `test_comparison_replay_boundaries.py` | 120 | Rehashed corrupt data, parallel comparison ordering and exit codes, memory ranges, failure-bundle and replay tampering |
| `test_model_boundary_matrix.py` | 98 | All FP comparison predicates, min/max NaN and ±0 selection, bitwise operations at every bit position, exact-fit memory access and guards |
| `test_studio_boundaries.py` | 62 | Corrupt history, start/stop/rerun, HTTP failure paths, UTC conversion, search/state updates/failure recovery in the actual UI JavaScript |
| `test_execution_boundaries.py` | 46 | Invalid model exports, load failures, cache isolation, fixture arguments, reverse worker-completion order, input immutability |
| `test_quality_boundaries.py` | 26 | Setup/teardown/import failures, discovering 0 tests, propagation of quality-gate failures, invalid progress-log values |
The new model matrices perform **45,408 direct output checks**. Their expectations come from IEEE encoding order,
logical operations, and explicit byte operations, without using Python float, the target comparator, or model helpers.
They validate every input without changing official case contracts.
Together with the existing independent oracles, there are 74,722 output checks. Some inputs are checked again,
so check counts must not be treated as counts of distinct inputs or instruction types.
The C file `tests/native/test_native.c` adds **2,582 input patterns** for this Mac's ARM and portable adapters.
They cover truncation at every byte position in 3 operations, NUL/invalid-byte injection,
every insufficient output capacity, exact-fit and excess capacities, leading/trailing guards, and restoration
of rounding and exception state from before the call. Truncated inputs are allocated in genuinely short regions
so ASan can detect out-of-bounds reads. These checks do not establish native conformance of the entire instruction suite.
Issues found by the reproducing tests were also fixed:
- Unwrapped exceptions for invalid types, deeply nested YAML, and NaN comparison policies; insufficient type checks on generator/fixture arguments.
- Incorrect acceptance of ISA contracts and failure-bundle diagnostics through `True == 1` / `False == 0`, and ignored input-ID context.
- Files left open after fsync failures in atomic writes, and recursion limits for long ISA references.
- Publication of failure bundles inconsistent with comparison results, and display of corrupt target-specific history.
- Invalid URLs, truncated HTTP bodies, disappearing processes during stop, and timestamps displayed outside UTC.
- Report creation interrupted by quality-class setup/teardown failures, and success reported when discovery found 0 tests.
Existing NaN/rounding model mismatches remain in the complete suite, so its overall exit code is not 0.
They are not suppressed with skips or expected failures; new tests and framework regressions are recorded separately.
Coverage percentages were not measured in this run.
The full run on this Mac (arm64 Darwin / Python 3.14.7) reported 2,159 model-output mismatches,
0 other assertion failures, 0 execution errors, and 0 skips. All added tests passed.
Both the ARM NEON wrapper and native ABI CTests passed in C Debug and ASan/UBSan builds.
To run only the additions (no extra Python dependencies; UI JavaScript checks require Node.js):
```sh
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*boundaries.py'
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_model_boundary_matrix.py
## Previously added exploratory cases
Official instruction contracts for the 254 case packs were retained. Added checks include input patterns with
independent expectations and framework rejection/comparison tests. Instruction-type counts and input-pattern counts differ.
| Added verification | Count | Coverage |
| Integer model inputs against expected outputs | 17,090 | Wrapping, saturation, signedness, multiplication, all imm8 values, 64-bit shift counts, lane order, memory boundaries |
| Floating-point model inputs against expected outputs | 10,708 | 107 instruction cases, 12 families, 4 rounding modes, NaNs, subnormals, rounding midpoints, conversion boundaries |
| Schema/artifact/replay/comparison tests | 291 methods | Closed schemas, tampering, symlinks, all status combinations, NaN policies, ULP, strict tolerances |
| CLI configuration-selection regressions | 4 methods | Automatic selection of old/new configuration files, quality enabled/disabled, explicit configuration-file controls |
Before the ARM/RISC-V additions, the complete verification run contained 495 test methods,
29,314 independent model-output checks, and 29,292 recorded distinct input IDs. It found 2,159 model mismatches,
13 other assertion failures, 0 execution errors, and 0 skips. Of the model mismatches, 106 were under official nearest-even contracts
and 2,053 were under validation-only rounding extensions. C sanitizer checks and the cross-build of 12 objects passed.
Integer expectations use unbounded integer arithmetic, explicit fixed-width encoding, and independent byte operations.
They are not generated by model operation helpers or the comparison engine.
For exhaustive imm8 checks on shuffle and shift operations, only inputs exceeding the original permitted values are
validated as `validated_immediate_extension`. The official immediate allowlists are unchanged.
Floating-point expectations were captured by a separate C program that does not import the model.
Each packed instruction receives different values per lane; scalar instructions receive different upper poison lanes on the two sides.
All 10,708 inputs in the new corpus are distinct; 10,704 were absent from the previous 504-row corpus.
The remaining 4 are shared control inputs. Every row was recaptured with strict-FP `-O0` and `-O2` builds
and matched its stored value exactly.
The additional FP tests reproduced 1,988 model-mismatch patterns on arm64 Darwin / Python 3.14.7.
Of these, 70 under official nearest-even contracts consist of 54 NaN-payload-selection findings and 16 invalid-operation NaN-sign findings.
The remaining 1,918 use validation contracts extended with the corresponding rounding modes.
These are more reproducing inputs for existing NaN and ignored-rounding defects;
the mismatch count is not a count of root causes. All 17,090 integer checks passed.
### Newly reproduced deficiencies and additional validation cases
- Supplying arrays or dictionaries for the 4 NaN-comparison-policy fields or `signed_zero` performs set membership
before checking for a string, leaking `TypeError` instead of `ValidationError`. This is reproduced by 10 tests.
- Used alone, `validate_result_record(..., input_record=...)` accepts a well-formed `input_id` that does not match
the specified input. This is reproduced by 1 test. Higher-level artifact validation and comparison reject the mismatch,
so this does not mean the ordinary comparison pipeline reports a false match.
The test requests stronger validation in the lower-level API, distinct from the specification-required checks in the higher-level path.
- The `Path(None)` failure after automatic configuration selection in `check --quality` was fixed alongside ARM/RISC-V support.
Regression tests cover omitted and explicitly selected old/new configuration files. The remaining other assertion failures number 11.
### Issues found and fixed by the ARM/RISC-V extension
- ARM/RV floating-point differences retained an `openpower` label in nested diagnostics.
It was replaced with the actual target name, and tests reproduce differences on both targets.
- Empty comparison sets skipped target-name validation. Intel itself, unknown names, and `None` are now rejected.
- Multitarget HTML accepted duplicate targets, targets differing from the summary, and inconsistent input counts,
potentially producing inconsistent Intel shared-path execution counts. Regression tests now reject these cases.
- Checks also cover compatibility with old PPC bundles and the old `ioitf` command, reload/recomparison of ARM/RV bundles,
and snapshot independence from file tampering after loading.
See [Native status](../documentation/native-status.json) for native tests.
ARM runs 4596 checks. RVV executes the same ELF at VLEN 128/256 and compares
254 operations × 3 inputs against observed SSE2 output. The 12 RVV NaN differences are recorded as architecture observations,
separately from portable-model defects.
Failures are not suppressed using `expectedFailure`, skips, or replacement expected values.
Schema-rejection exception leaks are caught and then asserted to be `ValidationError`,
distinguishing them from accidental execution errors in the tests themselves.
```sh
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_integer_boundary_models.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_fp_boundary_models.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_protocol_adversarial.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_comparison_adversarial.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_cli_adversarial.py -v
To independently recapture the FP expectations:
```sh
clang -arch x86_64 -O0 -msse2 -ffp-model=strict -Wall -Wextra -Werror \
tests/native/probe_fp_boundary.c -o /tmp/equilane-fp-boundary-probe
.venv/bin/python tests/build_fp_boundary_oracles.py \
--probe /tmp/equilane-fp-boundary-probe \
--execution-context 'x86_64 SSE2 under Rosetta on arm64 Darwin' \
--build-command 'clang -arch x86_64 -O0 -msse2 -ffp-model=strict -Wall -Wextra -Werror tests/native/probe_fp_boundary.c -o /tmp/equilane-fp-boundary-probe' \
--verify
The same `--verify` check also passes when the probe is built with `-O2`. Ordinary Python tests require neither a compiler nor Rosetta.
The corpus records the capture environment, compiler, build command, and SHA-256 hashes of the probe, sources, and all expectations.
These are SSE2 observations under Rosetta, not conformance evidence between physical Intel and OpenPOWER machines.
Specification references are the [Intel Intrinsics Guide](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/intrinsics-guide/index.html),
[Intel SDM](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html), and
[Floating-Point Reference Sheet](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/floating-point-reference-sheet-for-intel-architecture.html).
## Results verified before these additions
On arm64 Darwin / Python 3.14.7, **171 output-mismatch patterns** were reproduced.
These comprised the initial 36 findings plus 135 instances of ignored rounding modes.
There were 1,516 output checks, 17 output-verification test methods, and 1 oracle-provenance consistency method.
The mismatch count is not the number of bugs. The root causes fall into 3 groups: NaN signs, NaN payload selection,
and ignored rounding modes. The last group appears in 5 implementation paths.
| Detected difference | Mismatch patterns | Contract scope |
| Sign of NaNs produced by invalid operations | 12 | Official nearest-even |
| NaN payload selection | 24 | Official nearest-even |
| Requested rounding ignored in arithmetic | 56 | Validation-only rounding extension |
| Requested rounding ignored in square root | 8 | Validation-only rounding extension |
| Requested rounding ignored in floating-point-to-integer conversion | 37 | Validation-only rounding extension |
| Requested rounding ignored in f64-to-f32 conversion | 16 | Validation-only rounding extension |
| Requested rounding ignored in integer-to-floating-point conversion | 18 | Validation-only rounding extension |
Concrete examples with different rounding modes:
| Operation / setting | Input | SSE2 expectation | Model at the time |
| f32 sqrt / toward_positive | `0x40000000` (=2) | `0x3fb504f4` | `0x3fb504f3` |
The affected execution paths are `float_binary_case`, `sqrt_case`,
`conversion_case`, `scalar_conversion_case`, and `float_to_scalar_case` in `casepack_families.py`.
They ignore input `environment.rounding` and use host arithmetic or helpers fixed to nearest-even.
The official case declarations remain nearest-even. These 135 findings reproduce behavior when the supported modes
are extended; they do not claim the same differences occur under the official nearest-even contracts.
The 504 rounding-reference pairs are stored in `tests/data/rounding-oracles.json`.
`tests/build_rounding_oracles.py` captures them from an SSE2 probe without calling the Python model.
They cover positive/negative values in 4 modes, halfway values, underflow, overflow, integer boundaries, and upper scalar lanes.
Nearest-even and rounding-independent cvtt cases serve as controls.
The same 504 pairs were recaptured with strict-FP `-O0` / `-O2` builds and verified to match.
A further 768 checks move each of 128 bits, 1 bit at a time, through 6 bitcast operations.
Another 48 checks cover 3 unaligned stores at offsets 0–15, unused buffers, and leading/trailing guards.
No mismatches occurred in these 816 checks.
## NaN mismatches found in the initial run
Under Python on arm64 macOS, 4 of 10 test methods failed and 6 passed.
There were 36 failing subtests, arising from the following 2 causes. This stage included no implementation fixes.
| Example input (f64) | SSE2 expectation | arm64 model at the time |
1. NaNs generated by invalid operations have the wrong sign. This is reproduced in 12 combinations of
add / sub / mul, f32 / f64, and packed / scalar operations.
2. With a quiet NaN as the first argument and a signaling NaN as the second, the second argument's payload
is retained. This is reproduced in 24 combinations of add / sub / mul, f32 / f64, packed / scalar,
and the first argument's sign. Division and controls with the NaN order reversed pass.
The affected code is `float_binary_case.execute` in `src/equilane/casepack_families.py`.
Add / sub / mul convert bit patterns into Python floats and perform arithmetic on the host.
These official contracts require `bit_exact` without excluding such inputs, so the difference remains a mismatch
even when both values are NaNs. Ordinary fixtures miss it when both sides execute the same model.
Failures are not hidden with `expectedFailure` or skips. These tests are also included in the full unittest discovery,
so the complete suite exits with a code other than 0 on the unfixed arm64 environment.
Because the bugs depend on the host, Python on x86_64 may not produce the same failure count.
## How findings appear in the report
```sh
.venv/bin/python -m equilane check --project equilane.toml --quality --showcase-report
The “Independent model verification and failure locations” section of `showcase.html` displays model-output mismatches,
other assertion failures, and test-execution errors separately. Even if the fixture comparison is PASS,
a failed quality check puts `QUALITY CHECK FAILED` at the top of the report.
In the unfixed environment of this record, the command exits with a code other than 0 but still generates the report.
A report generated without `--quality` marks independent model verification as “Not performed.”
An output mismatch is a difference found by directly comparing with a fixed expectation, without `equilane.compare`,
after successful model execution of an input conforming to an official or explicitly stated validation contract.
It is classified as **a Python portable-model output mismatch, not a misclassification by the comparison or aggregation logic**.
The model itself is a development implementation in this repository; these findings do not mean that a bug
was found in physical OpenPOWER hardware. Nor do these results establish that the entire framework is defect-free.
Machine-readable records are in `gates.python_coverage` in `quality/summary.json`.
`--quality` executes independent tests, but coverage measurement is off by default.
Sources are traced only when `--coverage` is explicitly added. Without measurement, the percentage is `null`
and `coverage_collected: false` is recorded. The `python_coverage` key is retained for compatibility with existing artifacts.
- `failure_classification`: Counts of model mismatches, other assertion failures, and execution errors.
- `model_output_mismatches`: Each input, input ID, test ID, expected value, observation, and comparison method.
- `execution_environment`: The OS, CPU architecture, and Python version actually used.
- `evidence_sources`: SHA-256 hashes of oracle tests, model sources, and related files.
- `model_findings_by_family` / `model_findings_by_contract_scope`: Counts by cause family and contract scope.
- `model_oracle_checks_run`: Output checks performed, distinct from test-method count.
- `model_oracle_reference`: SSE2 record count, capture environment, and SHA-256 hashes of the probe and generation script.
- `model_oracle_references`: Sources for old/new corpora and independent integer expectations.
- `model_oracle_tracked_unique_inputs`: Distinct model-verification inputs with recorded input IDs.
- `test_assertion_failures` / `test_execution_errors`: Test IDs, exception names, and messages for findings other than model mismatches.
The NaN oracle comes from the SSE2 probe verification recorded in this document.
Quality checks use the fixed expectations without rerunning the probe.
To independently recheck the stored rounding references, build the probe above and then run:
```sh
.venv/bin/python tests/build_rounding_oracles.py \
--probe /tmp/equilane-probe-sse2-nan \
--execution-context 'x86_64 under Rosetta on arm64 Darwin' --verify
`--verify` compares the stored 504 pairs with recaptured results.
Remove `--verify` only when the references need updating. Ordinary tests also check the source SHA-256
to prevent silently using an old oracle after source changes.
The terminal quality metrics were also changed from displaying `tests_run` as `passed`
to displaying it as `executed`. This display issue is separate from the 36 model-output differences above.
The correction keeps execution counts distinct from pass counts.
## Additional boundary conditions
- Min / max: input order for ±0 and NaNs, and returning a signaling NaN in the second argument unchanged.
- Scalar arithmetic: exact bit preservation of upper-lane signaling NaNs, negative zero, and payloads.
- f64 → f32: immediately below, exactly at, and immediately above rounding midpoints; ties to even; underflow to zero;
subnormal/normal boundaries; overflow; negative values; zeroing unused lanes.
- Variable shifts: counts at least as large as the width, `2^32`, `2^32 + 1`, `2^63`, `2^64 - 1`,
and ignoring the count's upper 64 bits.
without mixing adjacent lane pairs.
## Verify NaN expectations with SSE2
`native/probe_sse2_nan.c` calls SSE2 intrinsics directly with runtime inputs.
FP exceptions are masked, rounding is nearest-even, and FTZ / DAZ are disabled.
It does not depend on the Python model.
For Apple Silicon + Rosetta:
```sh
clang -arch x86_64 -std=c11 -O0 -msse2 -ffp-model=strict \
tests/native/probe_sse2_nan.c -o /tmp/equilane-probe-sse2-nan
With Clang on x86_64, omit `-arch x86_64`.
```sh
/tmp/equilane-probe-sse2-nan f64 add 0x7ff0000000000000 0xfff0000000000000
/tmp/equilane-probe-sse2-nan f64 add 0x7ff8000000000042 0x7ff0000000000001
/tmp/equilane-probe-sse2-nan f32 mul 0x00000000 0x7f800000
These expectations were verified by executing x86_64 binaries under Rosetta.
They are not native conformance evidence between physical Intel and OpenPOWER machines.
Ordinary Python test execution requires neither a compiler nor Rosetta.
